question: The gravitational constant (G) was first measured by ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cavendish**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Henry Cavendish**, a **British scientist**, was the first person to successfully measure the **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)** in the laboratory. This landmark achievement took place between **1797 and 1798**.
 
• The experiment is famously known as the **Cavendish Experiment**. It involved the use of a **torsion balance** to measure the extremely weak gravitational attraction between two pairs of lead spheres.
 
• While **Sir Isaac Newton** had formulated the **Law of Universal Gravitation** in his work **Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica** in **1687**, he did not calculate the value of **G**. He only established the relationship that force is proportional to the product of masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance.
 
• The primary objective of Cavendish's experiment was actually to **"weigh the Earth"** by determining its **average density**. By finding the value of **G**, he was able to calculate the **Earth's mass** for the first time.
 
• The value **Cavendish** derived for the density of the Earth was **5.448 times** that of water, which is remarkably close to the modern accepted value of **5.515 g/cm³**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Isaac Newton:**
 
 
• **Newton** is credited with discovering the **Universal Law of Gravitation**, which states that every particle attracts every other particle in the universe with a force (F).
 
• The formula is **F = G(m1m2)/r²**, where **m1** and **m2** are masses and **r** is the distance between them. However, **Newton** did not have the experimental tools to measure the constant **G** himself.
 
 
 
• **Galileo Galilei:**
 
 
• **Galileo** was an **Italian astronomer and physicist** known as the "father of modern science."
 
• He performed experiments on **motion and free fall**, famously demonstrating that all objects, regardless of their mass, fall with the same **acceleration (g)** in the absence of air resistance. He did not measure the universal constant **G**.
 
 
 
• **Johannes Kepler:**
 
 
• **Kepler** was a **German astronomer** who formulated the **three laws of planetary motion** in the early **17th century**.
 
• His laws described the **elliptical orbits** of planets and the relationship between a planet's distance from the Sun and its orbital period, providing the empirical foundation for **Newton's** later work on gravity.
 
 
 
• **The Gravitational Constant (G):**
 
 
• The modern value of **G** is approximately **6.674 x 10^-11 N·m²/kg²**.
 
• It is a **scalar quantity** and is considered a **fundamental physical constant** in the universe, meaning its value is the same everywhere and at all times.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between G and g:**
 
 
• **G** is the **Universal Gravitational Constant** and remains constant throughout the universe.
 
• **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity**, which is approximately **9.8 m/s²** on the surface of the **Earth** but changes depending on the **altitude, latitude**, and the planet or celestial body one is standing on.
 
 
 
• **The Torsion Balance:**
 
 
• The **torsion balance** used by **Cavendish** was originally designed by the geologist **John Michell**, who died before he could complete the experiment. **Cavendish** rebuilt the apparatus and made it much more sensitive to eliminate errors caused by **air currents and temperature changes**.
